subtitle: Fortnightly intelligence for automotive distribution — Middle East and Europe
audience_note: Prepared for corporate strategy and senior leadership.
ai_notice: Items are screened from named public sources and summarised with AI assistance. The "Initial view" line is a first read intended to open discussion, not a settled position or a recommendation to act.
impact_coherence: Impact and action must agree. A high-impact item cannot sit at Unreviewed or No action — if nothing is being done about it, it is not high impact.

impact_criteria.high: Changes a decision we would otherwise take, or moves volume or gross profit in a market we sell in, within 12 months.
impact_criteria.medium: Informs planning or revises our read of a market, but forces no decision this cycle. Registration data and directional policy signals normally sit here.

filter_note: Countries and regional jurisdictions such as the EU and GCC are filterable; source markets — China, Japan, South Korea — appear as tags only, since they are where decisions are made rather than markets we distribute into.

regulation_trade.name: Regulation & Trade
regulation_trade.definition: Type approval and homologation, emissions and safety rules, tariffs and duties, rules of origin, local-content requirements, shipping and routing. Governs whether we can land, certify and legally sell a unit, and at what cost.

product_powertrain.name: Product & Powertrain
product_powertrain.definition: Model launches and facelifts, powertrain mix, specification suitability for regional climate and fuel quality, recalls and warranty exposure. Governs what reaches our showrooms and what it displaces in the existing line-up.

retail_aftersales.name: Retail & Aftersales
retail_aftersales.definition: Agency and dealer contracts, direct-to-consumer and online retail, showroom formats, used and certified pre-owned, fleet, finance and insurance — and separately, service networks, parts logistics, warranty terms and the ownership-economics annuity. Governs how we sell, and what we continue to earn after the sale.

competition_brand.name: Competition & Brand Moves
competition_brand.definition: Distribution agreements, market entries and exits, competitor franchise wins, registrations and market share, pricing and discounting, macro and consumer-credit conditions, grey and parallel imports. Governs the portfolio we can represent and the volume the market gives us.

charging_energy.name: Charging & Energy
charging_energy.definition: Charging network build-out, grid capacity and constraints, tariffs and incentives, fuel quality, observed EV adoption. An operating precondition: an EV franchise is worth only what the local energy infrastructure can support.

editions.label: 15 Jun '26 – 28 Jun '26
editions.editor_note: Pilot issue. Screening for this window was limited to two items that met our sourcing threshold, and no editorial ranking is applied. Both concern the European trade perimeter: the Commission moving to close the plug-in hybrid duty gap, and the registration data showing why that gap mattered.

items.headline: Commission prepares countervailing duties on Chinese plug-in hybrids
items.summary: Reporting indicated the European Commission had completed preparations for countervailing duties on plug-in hybrids imported from China, targeting manufacturers including BYD, Chery and SAIC. Battery-electric imports have carried manufacturer-specific duties since October 2024 — 17% additional for BYD, taking its total to 27% — while plug-in hybrids faced only the standard 10% tariff.
items.initial_view: Closing this gap would remove the arbitrage that made Chinese plug-in hybrids the cheapest electrified option in our European markets, and would reprice a segment we have been building volume in.

items.headline: EU registrations up 4% to May as battery-electric share reaches 20%
items.summary: ACEA reported EU car registrations up 4% in the year to May 2026, with battery-electric cars at 20% share against 15.3% a year earlier and 950,521 units registered over five months. Combined petrol and diesel share fell to 30.1% from 38%. Plug-in hybrid registrations reached 460,217 units.
items.initial_view: Plug-in hybrid volume at this scale is what makes the pending duty question material rather than technical. The petrol and diesel decline also sets the trade-in and residual-value backdrop for our European used operations.

editions.label: 29 Jun '26 – 12 Jul '26
editions.editor_note: Two threads open in this window and both run into the next edition. Hormuz war-risk pricing began moving again after a brief post-truce softening, and Chinese manufacturers pressed harder for European production capacity — BYD approaching Renault for a shareholding, and separately narrowing its search for an existing plant to buy.

items.headline: Hormuz war-risk rates climb again as three vessels attacked and IMO advises avoidance
items.summary: The Lloyd's Market Association said war-risk rates for Strait of Hormuz transits rose after three vessels were attacked, following a softening that had taken hull premiums to roughly 2% of vessel value after the June US-Iran memorandum of understanding. Market estimates put premiums at around 5% of hull value as the emerging norm. The IMO advised ships to avoid transiting until crew safety could be assured.
items.initial_view: The June truce did not hold long enough to rebase our shipping assumptions downward. A 5% norm on hull value, with an official advisory against transit, puts Gulf inbound cost and timing into active management rather than watchful waiting.

items.headline: Renault rejected two BYD approaches for a shareholding, French daily reports
items.summary: Les Echos reported that BYD sought an equity stake in Renault twice — first in 2024, again in autumn 2025 — seeking access to Renault's European plants in exchange for battery and electrified-powertrain technology. An insider described the intent as taking control. Renault refused both times, citing a principle of not entering such agreements in its core European market, having already deepened ties with Geely.
items.initial_view: Chinese manufacturers want European assembly badly enough to bid for ownership, and incumbents are refusing. Where they eventually build determines the landed cost of the brands we represent, so the pattern of who says yes is worth tracking closely.

items.headline: Electric vans pass the tipping point on model choice and running costs
items.summary: Transport & Environment reported electric light commercial vehicles reached 11% of the EU market in 2025 with registrations up 68% in a year. Buyers now have more battery-electric van models available than combustion or hybrid ones — 61 against 54 — and electric vans can offer up to 14% lower total cost of ownership than diesel equivalents. Adoption varies sharply: 32% in Denmark and 29% in Sweden against 5% in Italy and 9% in Spain.
items.initial_view: The economic argument for our electric van proposition now rests on total cost of ownership rather than subsidy, which changes how we sell it. The market-by-market spread also tells us where a fleet-led approach works and where it does not yet.

items.headline: BYD narrows second European plant search to Spain and France
items.summary: BYD's special adviser for Europe, Alfredo Altavilla, told the Reuters Automotive Europe conference in Frankfurt that a decision on acquiring an existing European plant was close, with Spain and France the leading candidates and proposed EU local-content rules driving the timing. It would be BYD's second European passenger vehicle site after Szeged in Hungary, where mass production is now expected in the fourth quarter. A previously announced plant in Türkiye remains on hold with no timeline.
items.initial_view: The Türkiye plant stalling matters more to us than the Spain-or-France question, since it removes a nearby supply point for a market we serve and leaves Turkish volume dependent on imports under the existing tariff regime.

items.headline: Lucid cuts deep to protect runway as PIF adds further funding
items.summary: Reporting on Lucid's position at the halfway point of 2026 described a company fighting for operational stability and financial runway, with the Public Investment Fund injecting a further $750 million in late June to support restructuring under a new chief executive. The Gravity was named 2026 World Luxury Car of the Year, and the Uber partnership now covers at least 35,000 vehicles with commercial deployment targeted for late 2026.
items.initial_view: The only manufacturer assembling vehicles in Saudi Arabia is restructuring under sovereign support. That shapes how quickly local assembly becomes a credible route for the brands we represent, and what the Kingdom will underwrite to get there.

editions.label: 13 Jul '26 – 26 Jul '26
editions.editor_note: This fortnight is dominated by cost of access rather than demand. Hormuz war-risk pricing reset the Gulf landed-cost base, while in Europe the tariff perimeter kept moving — Chinese brands now take roughly a third of the plug-in hybrid market that duties do not yet cover. Coverage is weighted toward Europe and the supranational layer; Gulf franchise and standards developments are under-represented and are a known gap in this cycle.

items.headline: Hormuz war-risk premiums reach 3–10% of hull value as tanker attacks resume
items.summary: War-risk insurance for Strait of Hormuz transits reached 3% to 10% of hull value, against 0.25% before the conflict, after Iran resumed attacks on vessels routing through Omani waters and struck two Adnoc supertankers. Iran declared the waterway closed again, and the IMO reported roughly 6,000 seafarers trapped while working to evacuate stranded vessels.
items.initial_view: Every unit we land in the Gulf now carries a war-risk cost in points of hull value rather than basis points, and both routings carry exposure — sanctions compliance to the north, interdiction risk to the south. Landed-cost models and delivery promises across the GCC look due for rebasing.

items.headline: Chinese brands take a third of Europe's plug-in hybrid market as duties near
items.summary: Registration data showed Chinese brands at roughly a third of European plug-in hybrid deliveries in June, led by BYD, Chery and Geely. Reporting indicated the European Commission is moving closer to countervailing duties on Chinese-built plug-in hybrids, subject to member-state approval.
items.initial_view: The powertrain gap that made Chinese hybrids cheap in Europe is closing. If duties land on a formula similar to battery-electric vehicles, our European hybrid pricing and volume assumptions would need reworking inside two quarters.

items.headline: EU car market up 5.7% in H1 2026 as battery-electric share reaches 20.7%
items.summary: ACEA reported 5.90 million new EU car registrations in the first half of 2026, up 5.7%. Battery-electric cars took 20.7% share against 15.6% a year earlier, hybrids 37.3% and plug-in hybrids 9.8%, while the combined petrol and diesel share fell to 29.7% from 37.8%.
items.initial_view: Sets the powertrain mix our European franchises must supply into. Petrol and diesel losing eight points of share in twelve months is the figure that bears on stock, specification and residual-value planning.

items.headline: EU tariffs cut China-built BEV share but Chinese brands keep growing
items.summary: Transport & Environment analysis found China-produced electric cars fell to 17% of the EU battery-electric market in the first quarter of 2026 from a 22% peak, driven mainly by Tesla, BMW and Volvo moving output to Europe. Chinese-brand imports continued to rise, as did imports of Chinese batteries.
items.initial_view: Tariffs appear to be redirecting where cars are built rather than who sells them. Chinese-brand volume in Europe keeps growing, which supports our European portfolio thesis while shifting the landed-cost assumptions underneath it.

items.headline: Commission publishes Electrification Action Plan with 46% target and V2G framework
items.summary: On 17 July the European Commission published its Electrification Action Plan alongside a proposed Emissions Trading System review and a legislative proposal on network charges. It set an indicative 46% electrification target for 2040 and committed to regulatory sandboxes for vehicle-to-grid projects.
items.initial_view: Signals the charging and grid rules our European markets will operate under, and opens a vehicle-to-grid services angle adjacent to vehicle sales that we do not currently price.

items.headline: EU charging capacity outpaces EV uptake in every member state except Malta
items.summary: Transport & Environment analysis found that by the end of March 2026 all EU member states except Malta met the AFIR requirement of 1.3 kW of public charging capacity per registered battery-electric vehicle, with bloc-wide capacity exceeding the fleet-based target by 180%. Public charge points reached 1.1 million by the end of 2025.
items.initial_view: Weakens charging availability as the stated blocker to EV volume in our European markets. On this reading the binding constraint is price and residual values rather than infrastructure.

items.headline: Farizon adds SV Sport to UK electric van range as dealer network builds
items.summary: Farizon launched a Sport version of its SV electric van in the UK, developed with authorised converter CPD Bodies and featuring a UK-developed exterior package. Distributor Jameel Motors continues building its UK franchise network, targeting experienced van and truck dealers rather than a high-volume footprint.
items.initial_view: Tests whether a converter-led specification strategy can win UK fleet business without the cost of a broad dealer network — relevant to how we would scale other electric light commercial franchises.
